parts:
Hi all

Already install stan 2.5. Great to see such a great program growing.

I have been working in a model that is in the process of the first publication. The first model is a  multivariate change point model. 

Now I am working on a extension from the first model, this extension is:
- include another growth model for a predictor (this works)
- make that the rate of change on the predictor predict the change point of the multivariate model.(this part doesnt work)

This means that a parameter predicts another parameter from multivariate normal distribution. I am having problems to specify this new prediction.
Stan gives me this error:
TRANSLATING MODEL 'mod_lkj_mv_1ch2' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'mod_lkj_mv_1ch2' with error message:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning (non-fatal): Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) contains a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
 You must call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
  Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression:
    get_base1(mub,k,"mub",1) ~ multi_normal_cholesky_log(...)
Warning (non-fatal): Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) contains a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
 You must call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
  Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression:
    get_base1(mu,i,"mu",1) ~ multi_normal_cholesky_log(...)
Warning (non-fatal): Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) contains a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
 You must call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the  

I am familiar with this errors, all my transformations are linear.

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Here is my full model syntax

data{
int n; 
int parmt;
int nsubj;
int nvars;    
vector[nvars] y[n]; // arrray of order y[n,nvars]
int id[n];
real x[n]; 
vector[parmt] pm[nvars]; 
cov_matrix[parmt] cov_vb;
cov_matrix[nvars] cov_vm;
vector[nvars] mm;
int n_bio; // new
real x_bio[n_bio]; // new
real y_bio[n_bio]; // new
real mm_bio; // new
}

transformed data{ // cholesky decompisition of prior covariances
cholesky_factor_cov[parmt,parmt] Lvb;
cholesky_factor_cov[nvars,nvars] Lvm;
Lvb <- cholesky_decompose(cov_vb);
Lvm <- cholesky_decompose(cov_vm);
}

parameters {
vector[parmt] b[nvars,nsubj]; // array of order b[nvars,nsubj,parmt]
//vector[parmt] mub[nvars]; // array of order mub[nvars,parmt]
corr_matrix[parmt] corr_b[nvars]; // correlation between bs, one cor matrix for each variable
corr_matrix[nvars] corr_y; // correlation between y variables
vector<lower=0, upper=100>[parmt] sd_b[nvars];
vector<lower=0, upper=100>[nvars] sd_y; //
vector[2] b_bio[nsubj]; // new
real<lower=0,upper=10> var_bio; // new
vector[2] mub_bio; // new
real<lower=0,upper=10> varb_bio[2]; // new
vector[2] reg[nvars];
real<lower=0,upper=10> var_mub4[nvars]; // new
}

transformed parameters {
vector[nvars] mu[n]; // vector of order mu[n,nvars]
cholesky_factor_cov[nvars,nvars] Ly;
cholesky_factor_cov[parmt,parmt] Lb[nvars];
vector[n_bio] mu_bio; // new
//vector[nsubj] mu_b4[nvars]; // new
vector[parmt] mub[nvars]; // array of order mub[nvars,parmt]

for(k in 1:nvars){
Lb[k] <- diag_matrix(sd_b[k]) * cholesky_decompose(corr_b[k]);}
Ly <- diag_matrix(sd_y) * cholesky_decompose(corr_y);

for (i in 1:n){ // this loops run the piecewise regression
for (k in 1:nvars){
mu[i,k] <- b[k,id[i],1] + b[k,id[i],2] * x[i];
if (x[i] > b[k,id[i],4])
mu[i,k] <- mu[i,k] + (b[k,id[i],3] * (x[i] - b[k,id[i],4]));
}}

for(j in 1:n_bio){
mu_bio[j] <- b_bio[id[j],1] + b_bio[id[j],2]*x_bio[j];}

// this is the regression from 1 parametr to another parameter, 
// probably this is causing the problem
for(k in 1:nvars){ 
for(j in 1:nsubj){
//mu_b4[k,j] <- reg[k,1] + reg[k,2]*b_bio[j,2];
//b[k,j,4] <- reg[k,1] + reg[k,2]*b_bio[j,2];
mub[k,4] <- reg[k,1] + reg[k,2]*b_bio[j,2];
}}

}

model{

corr_y ~ lkj_corr(1);
for(k in 1:nvars){
corr_b[k] ~ lkj_corr(1);}

for (j in 1:nsubj){
for (k in 1:nvars){
//mu_b4[k] ~ normal(mub[k,4],var_mub4[k]);
b[k,j] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mub[k], Lb[k]);
mub[k] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(pm[k], Lvb);
}}

for (i in 1:n){
y[i] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu[i], Ly);
mu[i] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mm, Lvm);}

y_bio ~ normal(mu_bio, var_bio);
mu_bio ~ normal(mm_bio, 10);

for(j in 1:nsubj){
b_bio[j] ~ normal(mub_bio,varb_bio);}

for(k in 1:2){
mub_bio[k] ~ normal(0,10);}

reg ~ normal(0,50);

}
